dimension_description: Brightness here refers to luminance, the light leaving or reflected by a surface per unit area in a given direction. It connects what your eye perceives on a screen or page to the photometric power behind it. Unlike illuminance on a desk, luminance belongs to the surface itself under stated conditions. Each item below specifies the scene and viewing context so the number has a clear meaning.

items.description: Deep intergalactic space away from stars and dust is functionally dark, with only stray photons from the cosmic background. The luminance is near zero for human perception even after dark adaptation. Instruments still register faint glows from zodiacal light and unresolved galaxies. This number expresses the ideal empty field reference for contrast.

items.name: Deep Space
items.summary_short: Deep intergalactic space away from stars and dust is functionally dark, with only stray photons from the cosmic background.

items.description: A moonless rural night sky under clear air provides this approximate surface luminance to the ground as seen by a dark adapted eye. It is dominated by starlight and airglow rather than artificial sources. Photographers call it a long exposure regime where noise matters. The value is a practical baseline for night vision performance.

items.description: Under a clear dark sky with no Moon, the brightest parts of the Milky Way lift the apparent sky glow above the deepest rural darkness by about an order of magnitude. Astrophotographers chase places with so little artificial light that this faint band becomes obvious to the eye. The number is still far below comfortable reading conditions. It represents a rich starlit sky rather than true empty darkness.

items.description: Strong auroral curtains can make the sky visibly luminous in green and red even while the ground remains mostly dark. The display feels bright because your eyes are adapted to night, not because the absolute luminance rivals daylight. Cameras with long exposures exaggerate the effect. The value is a plausible surface-brightness scale for a vivid aurora.

items.description: Landscapes lit by a full moon at high altitude reflect enough light to reach this luminance when viewed directly. Snow and pale rock can run higher because of albedo. For reading outdoors some people find it barely sufficient at peak lunar elevation. The number assumes clear skies and a bright moon near opposition.

The number ties ambiance to measurable output.

Their visual punch comes from color contrast and dark surroundings as much as from raw luminance. Urban streetscapes use this effect heavily in entertainment districts. The value is a representative bright-sign scale.

Polarization studies and skylight models both lean on this scale. The number is a representative midday value.

items.description: A lightning channel is a transient plasma column whose apparent luminance can rival or exceed the brightest man-made light sources. The pulse is brief, but the eye still experiences it as a violent flash because the number is so high. Cameras saturate easily on nearby strikes for exactly this reason. The value is an order-of-magnitude luminance scale for a bright return stroke.

items.description: The apparent luminance of Sirius as a disk is a modeling construct since the star is unresolved to the eye. As seen through a telescope with finite aperture, diffraction spreads the light into an Airy pattern. The central peak behaves as if it had an extremely high surface luminance. This number expresses that conceptual peak for comparison only.

items.description: The solar photosphere has an effective surface luminance of this order across visible wavelengths. It sets the reference for daylight vision and the upper bound of common sensors. Atmospheric scattering and eye safety make direct viewing unwise. The number is a standard astrophysical parameter for the Sun.

items.description: A core-collapse supernova photosphere can briefly reach this effective luminance as the ejecta expand and cool. The light curve evolves rapidly so the number applies only near peak brightness. Spectra are line rich and depart from a perfect blackbody, which is why this is a deliberately simplified comparison. The figure situates stellar explosions against the Sun on a surface basis.

items.description: A thermonuclear Type Ia supernova is also extremely bright, but its mechanism is different from core collapse. White dwarf disruption lets it reach a similar surface-brightness regime while producing a cleaner standardizable light curve. This sits above ordinary supernovae but below the rarest superluminous events. The value is a representative peak photosphere scale.

items.description: Superluminous supernovae are rare explosions that can outshine ordinary supernovae by orders of magnitude. They are often powered by unusually energetic progenitors or central engines, so this scale bridges the gap between common supernovae and gamma ray bursts. The number is a peak effective luminance, not a literal blackbody surface. It is the sort of event that keeps transient-astronomy surveys busy.

It helps fill the bright gap between supernovae and the most extreme gamma ray bursts. The event is short, violent, and very rare.

It is one step below the brightest long-burst examples in this chart.

units.description: Candela per square meter is the SI unit of luminance, linking photometric intensity to emitting area. It matches how displays and light boxes are specified. Using this base unit keeps comparisons between screens, walls, and skies consistent. All item values are recorded in this unit before conversion.
units.name: candela per square meter

units.description: Lux measures illuminance on a surface and relates to luminance by a factor near pi for a perfectly diffusing surface. In practice the mapping depends on reflectance and geometry, so treat converted values as scene dependent. Lux is convenient for workplace and architectural standards. The factor shown provides a common reference for diffuse assumptions.
units.name: lux

units.description: Foot candles are illuminance in the imperial system, equal to lumens per square foot. Historical lighting tables use this unit, especially in North America. Conversions follow from the square foot to square meter area ratio. The factor here aligns with the diffuse relation used for lux.
units.name: foot-candles

units.description: Nits are equivalent to candela per square meter and common for displays.
units.name: nits
